inputs.share_count_basis: 3,388,624,000 ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim report note 6). No dilutive potential shares (note 6(b)). The 78.6M restricted shares held for the Post-IPO Equity Incentive Plan and 13.6M held for the Alliance Retailers Benefits Plan are counted as outstanding because they will be delivered under the award plans; forward SBC is expensed in the flows and the count is held FLAT (charge once).
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 balance sheet: cash at bank and on hand RMB 5,173.6M (includes time deposits; interest income on them is stripped from the flows, so the whole pile belongs in the bridge). Bank and other borrowings 1,169.9 current + 556.7 non-current = 1,726.6; lease liabilities 10.7 + 7.3 = 18.0 (treatment A, in net debt). Net cash RMB 3,429.0M. Net cash has fallen from RMB 6.05bn at end-FY2023 (post-IPO) as dividends (RMB 1,345M over FY2024-25) and inventory build were funded from the cash pile while owner FCF stayed negative.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated P&L, 'Equity-settled share-based payment expenses': a CREDIT of RMB 26.15M (reversal of prior-year charges after performance conditions lapsed). H1 FY2026 expense RMB 18.3M (0.7% of revenue). No equity-award taxes disclosed (net-share settlement not used; the company buys shares in the market for the award trusts: RMB 96.2M FY2025, RMB 85.9M H1 FY2026, financing activities).
inputs.buyback_note: No share repurchases. Shares bought for the Alliance Retailers Benefits Plan trust (RMB 85.9M H1 FY2026) are award-plan funding, not a buyback; they are the cash counterpart of the SBC charge that is already expensed in the flows.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY/HKD 1.1748 (HKD per CNY) from Yahoo CNYHKD=X on 2026-10-23. Per-share values computed in CNY and multiplied by 1.1748 to HKD. No dual listing exists for a parity check; HKD is pegged to USD so the cross moves with USD/CNY (7.0-7.3 range implies 1.07-1.12 HKD/CNY at the 7.8 peg -- 1.1748 is consistent with USD/CNY ~6.65).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~6.5%, beta ~1.1 for a mid-tier baijiu name with high operating leverage -> CAPM cost of equity ~9.0%. Plus 1.0pp for the H-share/offshore-China regime discount (policy risk is priced by HK investors in the discount rate, not in A-share multiples) -> 10.0% cost of equity; net cash so WACC = cost of equity. The same 10% is used in all three scenarios: demand cyclicality and the destocking cycle are carried in the scenario flows and weights (bear 30%), not stacked in the discount rate a second time.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: leases as debt. Lease liabilities RMB 18.0M included in total_debt; no separate lease charge in the flows (right-of-use depreciation sits inside D&A). Lease cash is ~RMB 7M/yr -- immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no non-controlling interests on the balance sheet; profit for the year is fully attributable to equity shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, non-US, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file). ZJLD is a PRC baijiu producer, so none of the non-FCF routes apply; it is routed as 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'. CONTEXT: this is a mid-collapse valuation. Revenue halved FY2024 -> FY2025 (RMB 7,066.8M -> 3,650.5M) after the May 2025 PRC anti-extravagance rules and a sector-wide destocking cycle (channel inventory ~900-day turnover); management deliberately cut shipments in H2 FY2025 (H2 revenue only RMB 1,153M vs RMB 2,934M in H2 FY2024). H1 FY2026 revenue +2.0% and net profit +1.0% is a stabilisation signal, not a confirmed recovery. BASE YEAR: FY0 = FY2025 (RMB 3,650.5M) -- the trough, NOT the FY2024 peak; the driver paths recover from the trough and the base case does not regain the FY2024 peak within the 10-year horizon (FY2035 ~RMB 6.2bn). last_fcf = reported FCF -1,344.7 - SBC (-26.2) - interest income 169.3 = -1,487.8: owner FCF has been negative in every listed year (inventory build to RMB 9.6bn at 30 June 2026), so the forward flows are built from components (EBITDA margin, D&A, capex, tax, working capital) and the historical FCF is a record, not a base. EBITDA margins in the driver paths are OPERATING EBITDA before SBC and EXCLUDING interest income (the metrics EBITDA includes other income; FY2025 1,112.1 - 169.3 interest - (-26.2) SBC = 916.6 = 25.1%; FY2024 33.6%; FY2023 32.5%; FY2022 30.0%; H1 FY2026 ~35% on the seasonally strong half). FY2023 net income included a RMB 814.9M non-cash fair-value gain on pre-IPO preference shares, excluded from every base here; FY2022 negative equity (-RMB 3,815.2M) was the preference-share liability that converted at the April 2023 listing, a capital-structure artefact, so the equity CAGR is not used for growth selection. Consumption tax sits in cost of sales and is inside the margin. Cash tax 25% (PRC statutory; FY2025 effective 25.4%). Interest income is stripped because net cash (RMB 3.4bn) is many times any plausible FCF base; the cash pile is added once in the bridge. H1 FY2026 cash burn is already in the 30 June 2026 net cash; Year 1 = FY2026 full year, so half a year of the forecast overlaps the balance-sheet date (standard approximation, noted).

equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend approved, unpaid at 30 June 2026 (dividends payable)
equity_bridge.note: Interim report note 12 / 14(b): RMB 206.0M payable; a claim on the cash already counted in net cash.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle judgment: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR from the FY2025 trough (RMB 3,650M -> ~6,180M), which stays below the FY2024 peak; the historical CAGRs are collapse-distorted and unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 3yr CAGR -14.6% and EPS 3yr CAGR -27.6% (FY2022 -> FY2025) measure the policy-shock collapse, not a trend. Equity 3yr CAGR is undefined: FY2022 equity was -RMB 3,815M because of the pre-IPO convertible preference-share liability (RMB 10,254M) that converted at listing; FY2023 -> FY2025 equity grew 3.6%/yr. Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined because owner FCF was negative in every year (FY2022 -2,163.7; FY2023 -829.5; FY2024 -884.6; FY2025 -1,487.8 -- reported FCF less SBC less interest income).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (RMB M): FY2022 -2,163.7, FY2023 -829.5, FY2024 -884.6, FY2025 -1,487.8. FY2022 OCF carried RMB 936M of cash taxes paid; FY2023-24 reported FCF was already negative before the SBC (70.0 / 352.7) and interest-income (159.5 / 236.7) adjustments, which together took another RMB 230-590M per year. Inventory rose from RMB 5.1bn (FY2022) to 9.6bn (H1 FY2026), 2.6x FY2025 revenue -- the cash the P&L reports as profit has gone into aged base liquor.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +12%: H1 was +2.0% (RMB 2,546M); H2 compares against the deliberate-destocking trough of RMB 1,153M, so a return to merely 60% of H1 shipment levels (RMB 1,540M) gives +12% for the year. Thereafter 8% -> 3% as the sub-premium tier recovers slowly; FY2035 revenue ~RMB 6.2bn, still below the FY2024 peak of 7.07bn.
base.margin_note: Operating EBITDA pre-SBC, ex-interest income. FY2025 was 25.1% (trough, fixed costs over halved volume); FY2023-24 ran 32.5-33.6%. Base matures at 32%, below the prior peak, because ASP has reset (RMB 285k -> 249k/ton) and the Premier Retailers Alliance shares margin with the channel.
base.da_capex_note: D&A ~RMB 360M/yr on PP&E of RMB 5.1bn, roughly flat in absolute terms so falling as a % of growing revenue. Capex RMB 459M in FY2025 (RMB 1.08bn FY2024); seven facilities already built and volumes half of capacity, so capex converges on D&A plus modest growth (6.8% vs D&A 6.2% in the terminal year).
base.wc_note: Negative capture: an inventory-heavy distiller (inventory 2.6x revenue, receivables small, payables large) consumes cash as revenue grows. -40% of the revenue change is below the historical inventory/revenue ratio (~0.9-1.0x in FY2022-24) because the RMB 9.6bn base-liquor stockpile can absorb part of the recovery without new build.

bull.growth_note: Sector destocking completes in 2026, Li Du's national expansion sustains double-digit growth, Zhen 15 relaunch and Da Zhen restore the sauce-aroma core; FY2024 peak revenue regained in FY2033 (the eighth forecast year), FY2035 ~RMB 7.6bn. Margin recovers past the prior peak to 34% on self-produced base liquor and premium mix.

bear.growth_note: The H1 FY2026 stabilisation is a restocking blip: sector channel inventory (~900 days) forces a second leg down in FY2027-28, anti-extravagance norms and the generational shift away from baijiu permanently shrink the sub-premium tier, and revenue stagnates near RMB 3.8bn. Margin settles at 23% with price inversion and fixed-cost under-absorption; D&A on an over-built asset base stays ~10% of revenue. The engine cannot book inventory write-downs; they would be on top of this.

scenario_narratives.base: The May 2025 policy shock and sector destocking have reset ZJLD to a lower base, from which it recovers slowly rather than snapping back. FY2026 grows ~12% almost entirely because H2 FY2025 was a deliberate shipment-cut trough; thereafter growth fades from 8% to 3% as Li Du's national expansion offsets a structurally smaller Zhen Jiu gifting/banquet market. Operating EBITDA margin climbs from 29% to 32%, short of the 33-34% of FY2023-24 because ASP has reset and the Premier Retailers Alliance shares more margin with retailers. Capex falls toward D&A on an already over-built seven-plant footprint, and the inventory build slows but growth still consumes working capital. FY2035 revenue of ~RMB 6.2bn remains below the FY2024 peak; the valuation does not extrapolate that peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: Destocking completes in 2026 and the sector's 2025-26 contraction proves cyclical: official-consumption restrictions bite less on the private banquet, wedding and gifting occasions ZJLD's Da Zhen and Zhen 15 relaunch target, Li Du's +29% H1 FY2026 momentum carries nationally, and the Premier Retailers Alliance delivers disciplined pricing and channel profitability. Revenue regains the FY2024 peak by FY2033 and reaches ~RMB 7.6bn by FY2035; margin rises to 34% as self-produced base liquor replaces purchased liquor and the mix premiumises. Working-capital drag eases as aged stock is sold down.
scenario_narratives.bear: The industry-wide channel inventory (~RMB 300bn, ~900-day turnover) means the H1 FY2026 uptick was restocking, not demand; even Moutai's 2026 price rise failed to lift the sector. A second leg down in FY2027-28 takes revenue below RMB 3.4bn, the anti-extravagance regime and younger consumers' drift from baijiu make the sub-premium tier structurally smaller, and a new CEO (June 2026) is managing a shrinking business with RMB 9.6bn of inventory that may need writing down. Margin settles around 23% with fixed-cost under-absorption; the dividend is cut. Net cash keeps the company solvent, which is why the scenario is a stagnation case rather than a going-concern case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: the sector downturn is unresolved (channel inventory ~900 days, sector sales still falling in H1 2026), the thesis rests on an unproven turnaround under a new CEO, and there is a plausible structural (generational, policy-regime) component to the demand loss. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right: sector destocking completing, Li Du sustaining national double-digit growth, and the Zhen Jiu core returning to growth with margin above the prior peak. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ZJLD is valued mid-collapse, from the FY2025 trough rather than the FY2024 peak. Revenue halved in one year on a policy shock that hit the entire baijiu sector, and H1 FY2026's +2% is a stabilisation signal, not a recovery. The base year is FY2025 revenue (RMB 3,650M) with a component-built margin path that recovers from the 25% trough toward 32% operating EBITDA -- below the 33-34% of FY2023-24 because ASP has reset. Historical owner FCF is negative in every listed year (reported FCF less SBC less interest income), because profits have been reinvested in RMB 9.6bn of aged base liquor and dividends were funded from IPO cash; the forward FCF is therefore built from components and not from any historical FCF, and the working-capital capture is negative so growth consumes cash. WACC is 10% in CNY (CAPM ~9% plus 1pp for the offshore-China/policy regime) applied equally to all scenarios; the demand-cyclicality and regulatory risk is charged in the scenario flows and in a 30% bear weight, not stacked in the discount rate. Terminal value is capped at 15x FCF for a cyclical with a structural question mark; Gordon at 10%/2.5% binds at ~13.7x. Net cash of RMB 3.4bn (30 June 2026) is added once, with interest income stripped from the flows and the RMB 206M unpaid FY2025 dividend deducted. The result sits well below the market price: at the current price the market capitalises ~43x FY2025 earnings and ~24x consensus FY2026, i.e. it is pricing a return to FY2024-level earnings within two to three years, which neither the sector data nor H1 FY2026 supports. Book value is ~HKD 4.8/share, of which RMB 9.6bn of inventory at cost is 70%; the DCF below book says the stockpile only earns its cost of capital if it is sold through at recovered prices, which is the bull case.
key_risks_to_valuation: Pace and depth of the baijiu sector recovery: the base case's FY2026 +12% leans on an easy H2 comparison; if H2 FY2026 shipments do not normalise, FY2026 lands near the bear case.

Inventory: RMB 9.6bn (2.6x revenue) of mostly aged base liquor; the engine cannot model write-downs, and continued production ahead of sales is an ongoing cash drain beyond the working-capital capture assumed.
Margin reset: ASP fell 13% FY2024 -> FY2025 and the Premier Retailers Alliance shares channel margin; the 32% mature margin could be optimistic if price inversion persists.
Policy regime: a further tightening of anti-extravagance or consumption-tax rules would hit demand and margin simultaneously; a relaxation is the upside.
Brand concentration (Zhen Jiu + Li Du ~82% of revenue) and management transition (new CEO June 2026).
Currency: value is built in CNY and translated at CNY/HKD 1.1748; a weaker RMB lowers the HKD value one-for-one.
